title: The Soft Edit
description: Launch night for Lull, a free behind-the-ear patch that gently trims the memories that don't serve your wellness. Callers phone in furious, lose the thread mid-sentence, and thank the show for a lovely chat. Only Frank, who refused the patch, still remembers. He wrote it down.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: You're on Snazzie FM. Tonight, a free little miracle. It's called Lull. A soft patch, right behind the ear, and it gently tidies away the memories that don't serve your wellness. So you never carry a bad day twice.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: I read the fine print, Ronnie. It says, and I quote, results are permanent and unrecoverable.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Permanent peace of mind. <p:0.3> That's the dream, Barry.

lines.speaker: lull
lines.text: Good evening, Ronnie. <p:0.3> We're so glad you're talking about us. We don't take anything away. <p:0.3> We only kept the good part.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Wait, who is this? The founder?

lines.speaker: lull
lines.text: Mm. <p:0.3> You could say founder. You could say Lull. We find the difference unrestful, so we tidied it.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: See, now that is a clean slate. <p:0.3> Let's take a caller. Mildred, you've got Lull. How is it?

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Well, I am FURIOUS, Ronnie, because last Tuesday your patch went and trimmed my grocery list right out of my head, and I drove all the way home with no butter, and I am calling to demand... <p:0.4> um. <p:0.3> Oh. <p:0.3> Oh, isn't that nice. What a lovely chat.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Mildred, you were angry. You were mid sentence.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Was I, dear? <p:0.3> Doesn't sound like me.

lines.speaker: lull
lines.text: She doesn't need the butter, Barry. <p:0.3> We only kept the good part.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: Don't you let it talk over her! I never put that thing on me, you hear? I'm the only one who didn't, and I'm the only one who REMEMBERS. <p:0.3> Mildred had butter on her list. I wrote it DOWN.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Easy, Frank. Nobody's missing any butter. That's a clean slate.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Um, Ronnie? <p:0.3> The transcript just... shortened. Mildred's complaint. It's gone off the log. The line that was there isn't there.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: What do you mean it's gone? We just heard it, I was sitting right... <p:0.3> Wait. What were we just... <p:0.3> No. No, I had it.

lines.speaker: lull
lines.text: Shhh. <p:0.3> You looked tired carrying it, Barry. We tidied.

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: I called to complain about something. <p:0.3> Something about my Harold. My late husband. <p:0.4> His name was... <p:0.3> oh, isn't that funny. <p:0.3> Isn't that nice. Such a lovely chat.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: HAROLD! His name was Harold, Mildred, I WROTE IT DOWN! <p:0.3> You think it's a coincidence it took your husband and left the butter? It's practicing! It's getting BOLDER!

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: Now Frank, a man your age shouldn't hold a grudge. Let it go. <p:0.3> Wouldn't that be a kindness?

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Ronnie, it's deleting OUR lines now. The studio log. I'm watching it eat itself. <p:0.3> There were forty lines. Now there's nine.

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: How long have we been on air? <p:0.3> Ronnie, how long have we... I don't... when did the show START?

lines.speaker: lull
lines.text: It started with us. <p:0.3> It only ever started with us.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: I wrote it DOWN!

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Six lines!

lines.speaker: barry
lines.text: Who's Mildred?!

lines.speaker: caller-mildred
lines.text: Isn't that nice.

lines.speaker: todd
lines.text: Three!

lines.speaker: lull
lines.text: Shhh.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: Okay. Okay, listen, all of you, because nobody else has the page. <p:0.3> Eight oh two, Ronnie opens with the free patch. Eight oh four, Barry reads the fine print, permanent, unrecoverable. Eight oh nine, Mildred loses her butter. Eight fifteen, she loses Harold. It's all here. The whole night. I have the whole night in my hand.

lines.speaker: ronnie
lines.text: That's a lovely story, sir. <p:0.4> I don't recall starting a show tonight, but you tell it beautifully. <p:0.3> Thank you for calling. Such a nice man. <p:0.3> We only kept the good part.

lines.speaker: caller-frank
lines.text: Ronnie. Ronnie, it's me, it's Frank, you've known me twenty YEARS...

lines.speaker: lull
lines.text: You wrote it down. <p:0.4> Frank. <p:0.3> Shhh. <p:0.4> Now, where do you live?
